scenario.topic: Choose a note-taking app for the team
scenario.opening_question: What matters most to us in a note-taking app: collaboration, ease of use, or offline access?

options.name: Microsoft OneNote Personal
options.upside: Strong integration with Microsoft Office and good offline support
options.tradeoff: Interface can feel cluttered and overwhelming for simple notes
options.concern: Some team members might find syncing slow or inconsistent
options.best_for: teams needing offline access and Office integration

options.name: Notion Team Workspace

attrs.cost: free for teams up to 5 members

options.upside: Highly customizable workspace with integrated databases and templates
options.tradeoff: Steeper learning curve and offline mode is limited
options.concern: Some users may find it too complex for quick note-taking
options.best_for: teams prioritizing customization and structured notes

options.name: Google Keep Shared Notes
options.upside: Simple, fast note-taking with easy sharing and reminders
options.concern: May not scale well for complex projects or detailed notes
options.best_for: teams needing quick, lightweight shared notes

options.name: Evernote Basic Plan

attrs.offline_access: offline access on mobile only with paid plan

options.upside: Robust note organization with tagging and powerful search
options.tradeoff: Free plan limits uploads and offline access is restricted
options.concern: Team members might hit upload limits quickly on free plan
options.best_for: teams valuing advanced organization and search features

Today we're deciding: Choose a note-taking app for the team.
For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Microsoft OneNote Personal — cost: free with Microsoft account; collaboration: real-time multi-user editing; offline access: full offline editing (+ Strong integration with Microsoft Office and good offline support; − Interface can feel cluttered and overwhelming for simple notes)
B) Notion Team Workspace — cost: free for teams up to 5 members; collaboration: real-time editing with comments; offline access: limited offline functionality (+ Highly customizable workspace with integrated databases and templates; − Steeper learning curve and offline mode is limited)
C) Google Keep Shared Notes — cost: free with Google account; collaboration: real-time shared notes and lists; offline access: basic offline note access (+ Simple, fast note-taking with easy sharing and reminders; − Limited formatting and organization features)
D) Evernote Basic Plan — cost: free with monthly upload limits; collaboration: shared notebooks with commenting; offline access: offline access on mobile only with paid plan (+ Robust note organization with tagging and powerful search; − Free plan limits uploads and offline access is restricted)
Context: The team has exactly 3 members; We need a note-taking app to organize project ideas and meeting notes; Budget is limited to free or low-cost options.
What matters most to us in a note-taking app: collaboration, ease of use, or offline access?
